votes.reason: The structural claim is verified: old ss_e_op_custom emplaces each input polyline twice into m[0]/m[1] (f likewise) with cut::nothing, so m[0].size() == MALE.size() and there is no 2-point marker; the current custom_outlines concatenates all pairs into one Polyline per face and appends a synthetic {front, back} 2-point marker with edge_insertion. The geometry lens confirms this changes the produced plate outline, not merely the container shape. Old merge_joints dispatches on m[0][1].size() (the duplicated outline's own point count) and reads only entries [0] and [1]: (a) a 2-point custom outline: old joint line = (o[0],o[1]), inserted run = o; current marker = (o.front,o.back) = o, inserted run = o. Identical result. (b) a 5-point custom outline: old goes to case(5) (closed-path clipping via intersection_closed_and_open_paths_2D on .front()); current marker has 2 points so it goes down the line path and inserts the 5-point loop as an edge run with a degenerate front==back joint line. Different geometry. (c) any other point count (3, 4, 6+): old hits default: continue and merges nothing (and the hole passes emit only cut::hole entries, which custom never sets), so the plate outline is unchanged; current inserts the outline as an edge insertion. Different geometry. (d) k>=2 pairs: old reads only pair 1 (indices [0],[1]); pairs 2..k are never consumed by any pass, so the finding's phrase 'lose their separation' is inaccurate (the old never produced separate cuts for them), but the current concatenating them into one run still produces different geometry (pairs 2..k now enter the cut, joined by straight segments). Hence the claimed structural difference does change output for every custom outline except a single 2-point pair. The nothing -> edge_insertion type change itself is inert in both merges (old reads only hole/drill, current reads only hole/drill). Not refuted.
